author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two bright blue pillars rose from the summit of Mount Washington this week, turning New England’s highest peak into a memorial for the nearly 3,000 people killed in the September 11, 2001, attacks. The lights operated for two nights around the 25th anniversary, with the Mount Washington Auto Road offering summit shuttles for visitors who wanted to see the display up close.

Portsmouth organizer Renee Plummer began pursuing the project after last year’s anniversary and spent about a year securing permits and permissions. Malloy Events of Rochester served as the technical producer. The paired beams were designed to evoke the World Trade Center towers while honoring civilians, firefighters, police officers and other first responders who died in the attacks.

Fog limited some early views, but organizers anticipated clearer conditions Friday night. Visitors included firefighters and other first responders, and Auto Road staff described the mood at the summit as reflective. The completed display marked a new phase for a project that had already drawn attention over its possible effects on migrating birds: for attendees, the focus shifted to remembrance and the scale of seeing the beams rise from the mountain.
dek: Two pillars of light from New England’s highest peak gave visitors and first responders a place to mark the attacks’ 25th anniversary.
headline: Blue beams turn Mount Washington into September 11 memorial
